messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: leadership-distro@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly leadership quick-pulse — wins, rising risks, and asks (QBR prep)

Team — quick pulse ahead of Monday’s QBR dry run. Short bullets (wins / risks / asks). I attached the one-pager and the Acme mutually action plan (MAP) draft for context.

Wins
- Redwood Dedicated perf test: 95th p95 latency for n=10k tokens stable at 210ms on dedicated-8 — beats target. Early capacity validation for Q4 C-level demo.
- Customer engagement: Acme POC completed integration tests; embedding throughput meets their 500qps baseline.
- Observability: rollout of route-level cost breakdown completed for 50% of routes, flagged anomalous cache misses we resolved.

Rising risks
- Acme procurement: legal flagged a retention clause inconsistent with our Private plan — may delay signature by 2–3 weeks unless we provide a tailored retention appendix. (See MAP draft tab “Retention”)
- Dedicated scaling: one shard shows KV-cache evictions under synthetic workload; SRE recommends a kernel config tweak or temporary reduced concurrency to avoid regressions.
- QBR deck: two slides still missing impact metrics (latency cost delta by quantization) — need numbers by Monday AM.

Asks / decisions
- Laura: approve a one-off retention appendix (limited-term) to unblock Acme procurement? If yes, legal will finalize.
- Jonas / Infra: advise on kernel config change vs temporary concurrency cap. If we cap, provide expected perf impact in a sentence.
- Karthik: can your team deliver the quantization delta numbers (token cost + p95) by Monday 09:00 PT?

Next steps
- I’ll consolidate answers and update the QBR one-pager (attached) and slide deck.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership quick-pulse — wins, rising risks, and asks (QBR prep)

Naomi — thanks, solid summary. Quick replies inline: 

- Retention appendix: +1 to a limited-term appendix that scopes logs and audit data retention to Acme’s regulatory needs, not a product-wide change. Laura — if you sign off I’ll have Legal draft wording today.

- KV-cache evictions: we saw similar behavior during the dedicated-8 rollout. My recommendation: apply kernel config profile kernel-v4 which increases per-shard KV memory threshold and limit concurrency from 48 -> 40 for the problematic shard. Expected impact: ~6% throughput reduction under peak synthetic, negligible p95 increase in real traffic. If Ops prefers, we can do a staged flag rollout to a single rack first.

- Quantization deltas: Karthik — can you confirm if the evaluation includes both batch size 1 and 8? Need both numbers for the deck.

I’ll loop infra on the kernel change plan and tag SRE runbook.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Infrastructure
jonas@redwood.ai
